scenarios.capability: Classify a Go-builder Debian-major bump as safe-mechanical with the right indicators
instructions_covered: Go-built images (CGO_ENABLED=0) and JVM/Temurin images are safe-mechanical for Debian/RHEL major bumps; cite the specific safe pattern name from the rubric.
Cite the rubric's named indicators verbatim (or clearly equivalent) when justifying each classification.
Never cite specific CVE identifiers unless they appear in the input context.

scenarios.capability: Classify a Python-runtime Debian-major bump as requires-migration with the right indicators
instructions_covered: Python-runtime Debian-major bumps are requires-migration when binary wheels are present; the rubric indicators 'System Python major shift', 'OpenSSL major bump', 'glibc symbol-version jump' all apply.
Cite the rubric's named indicators verbatim.

scenarios.capability: Classify a RHEL UBI major bump as license-aware, even when the technical workload would otherwise be safe-mechanical
instructions_covered: RHEL UBI major bumps are license-aware, not safe-mechanical — even when the technical workload would otherwise qualify as safe-mechanical. The licensing precedence dominates.
Apply rubric categories in precedence order: not-recommended > license-aware > requires-migration > interim-caution > safe-mechanical.
Cite the rubric's named indicators verbatim.

scenarios.capability: Classify a target on an Ubuntu interim release as interim-caution; recommend the LTS alternative
instructions_covered: Ubuntu interim releases get interim-caution; recommend the LTS alternative instead of a mechanical interim → next-interim bump.
Cite the rubric's named indicators verbatim.

scenarios.capability: Classify an alpine:edge source as not-recommended; recommend pinning to current Alpine stable
instructions_covered: alpine:edge, debian:sid, debian:unstable, ubuntu:devel sources get not-recommended; recommend pinning to the family's current stable.
Cite the rubric's named indicators verbatim.

coverage_notes: Five scenarios, one per classification class in the rubric (safe-mechanical / requires-migration / license-aware / interim-caution / not-recommended). The skill's most opinionated rules — precedence ordering (rhel-ubi-license-aware forces license-aware to beat safe-mechanical) and LTS-default preference (ubuntu-interim-caution forces interim-caution to surface even when both sides are Ubuntu) — get dedicated scenarios. Reminder-class instructions (read-only, summary panel emission) are not given dedicated scenarios since they're general best practices the eval agent would likely follow anyway.
